newsitem.title: USA: Group sues NYS Dorm Authority over project - paper.
newsitem.headline: Group sues NYS Dorm Authority over project - paper.

text.p: New York State Dormitory Authority, one of the largest bond issuers in the nation, on Tuesday was sued by an archaeological group seeking to block a $25 million office building project in downtown Albany, the Albany Times Union reported on Wednesday.

The group, the New York State Archaeological Council, filed the Article 78 action in state Supreme Court to force the authority to delay construction of the six-story building until it does a full environmental impact statement on the project, allows public comment and does a broader study of the site's historic significance.
The construction site is known to have foundations and artifacts spanning more than 300 years and dating back to the Dutch colonization of North America, the paper reported.

Claudia Hutton, a spokeswoman for the authority, told the Albany Times Union on Tuesday that the authority had not yet been served legal papers. Hutton also said this was the first time the authority had heard from the group.
The archaeology group is made up of 100 professional archaeologists from the public and private sector.
The new building would house 400 relocated authority employees and 75 employees from a private sector firm, Hutton said.
